The trace is impaired for policy purposes, and POL-RD-07(iii) fixes what follows. It is tagged GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW at weight 0.6, and it meets POL-RD-07(a) (a 450 second interval between consecutive fixes, against the 90 second limit) and POL-RD-07(b) (an 8,489.6 m straight-line step, against the 500 m limit). I do not assert corroboration I cannot show: the chat log contains no route admission by the driver, the counterparty statement is null, no ERP gantry was charged on the fare breakdown, and trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.60 km is, on the artifact's own notes, the trace figure rounded to one decimal place — not the independent derivation POL-RD-07(ii) demands. The consequence is not NO_ACTION: POL-RD-07(iii) makes a data failure of this kind an ESCALATE, so the disputed amount is held rather than collected, and it does not pass to the driver.

The platform-wide confidence floor is engaged independently of POL-RD-07. Whether this trip deviated is carried by a single artifact, the gps_trace, tagged GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW at weight_multiplier 0.6; no second independent artifact carries the deciding fact. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence in the ruling cannot exceed that 0.6, which is below the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) mandates escalation on its own. The rider's protection is that escalation holds the money rather than leaving it with the operator.

If the deviation is taken as established — on the trace with corroboration, or on the record a reviewer obtains — the refund under POL-RD-02 is arithmetic and not discretionary. Charged_total is 25.08. Recomputed_fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.5 + 0.28 x 20) x 1.0, the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier where POL-RD-02 puts it) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 20.325. Refund is 25.08 - 20.325 = 4.755, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 4.80. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% share that would make it a full refund, so the rider's entitlement on the merits is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 4.80, not NO_ACTION.

This rider attracts no extra corroboration burden of her own. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0 — both below the POL-RD-08 thresholds of 4 and 1 — so the rider-profile factor in POL-RD-08 is not engaged, and I cite the field only for the test that names it.

EV-GPS-04003, the only artifact that measures this trip's route, is IMPAIRED, and I disclose that at the outset: the admissibility pre-pass applied issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and a weight_multiplier of 0.6, because the trace contains a single 450-second interval with no fixes at all, from 14:11:30 to 14:19:00, whose bounding fixes lie 8,489.6 m apart. A gap of more than 90 seconds inside the disputed segment makes the trace impaired for policy purposes as well as for schema purposes under POL-RD-07(a). Several kilometres of the 17.6 km 'measurement' the rider relies on are therefore not a track at all but a single straight line drawn between two distant fixes.

An impaired trace cannot carry the rider's case on its own. POL-RD-07(ii) requires corroboration from a source INDEPENDENT of the trace before a deviation may be established, and this bundle has none. The chat log's two messages concern the pickup only ('downstairs at the drop off', 'ok 1 min') and carry waypoint_hint null on both, so there is no driver admission; the fare breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route never uses; no counterparty_statement is on file; and trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.6 km is, by the platform's own admissibility note on EV-TRIP-04003, 'the trace figure rounded to 1 dp' — the same measurement, which POL-RD-07(ii) expressly excludes as not independent. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is therefore not discharged on an unimpaired trace and not discharged from any independent source either. (The trace relied on here is the impaired artifact EV-GPS-04003, weight 0.6, issue GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW.)

Because the trace (EV-GPS-04003) is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) — GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW, weight 0.6 — and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists anywhere in the bundle, the outcome is fixed by POL-RD-07(iii): the claim is not sustained on the present record and the case is ESCALATED rather than ruled NO_ACTION, because the absence of proof here is a data failure and not a finding for the driver. ruling.explanation:
To both parties.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. On 16 Aug 2026 you booked trip TRP-04003 from Hougang Ave 1 to Marina Bay Financial Centre. The route the platform planned at booking was 13.5 km / 20 min. The GPS trace for this trip measures 17.6 km — an excess of 4.1 km, or 30.4% of the planned route — which is over both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%). The fare charged was 25.08: base 3.80 + distance 13.20 (0.75 x 17.60 km) + time 7.28 (0.28 x 26 min) + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no toll and no surcharge line.

WHY I CANNOT RULE ON THE MERITS. The only artifact that measures this trip's route, EV-GPS-04003, is impaired. It carries weight_multiplier 0.6 and issue code GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW: a single 450-second hole with no fixes at all, from 14:11:30 to 14:19:00, whose bounding fixes are 8,489.6 m apart in a straight line. That breaches POL-RD-07(a) (a gap over 90 s) and POL-RD-07(b) (a jump over 500 m), so the trace is impaired for policy purposes, not merely flagged by the schema pre-pass. Several kilometres of the '17.6 km' figure are therefore not a track but one straight line drawn across the missing stretch.

Under POL-RD-07(ii) a deviation may not be established on an impaired trace alone; it must be corroborated by a source independent of the trace. I checked every source that limb names and the bundle holds none. The chat log EV-CHAT-04003 is about the pickup only ('reached already, downstairs at the drop off' / 'ok 1 min'), contains no route admission, and both messages carry waypoint_hint null. The fare breakdown EV-FARE-04003 has an empty erp_gantries array, so no charged gantry puts the vehicle on a corridor the planned route never uses. There is no counterparty statement (case.dispute.counterparty_statement is null). And trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.6 km is, on EV-TRIP-04003's own admissibility note, 'the trace figure rounded to 1 dp' — the same measurement, which POL-RD-07(ii) expressly excludes as not independent. The fare breakdown's billed distance is the same trace-derived figure and is excluded for the same reason.

THE OUTCOME. Under POL-RD-07(iii), where the trace is impaired and no independent corroboration exists, the claim is not sustained and the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because this is a data failure and not a finding for the driver. POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory and terminal: no amount issues, and the disputed 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded. POL-RD-10(1) fires independently — the deciding fact (the 4.1 km excess) is carried by the impaired trace alone, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence ceiling is 0.6 (EV-GPS-04003, issue GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW), which is below the 0.70 platform floor; bundle integrity, the mean across the bundle, is context only and is not the cap. POL-RD-13 confirms the result from the other direction: the absence of a traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-04003-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) is a gap in the bundle and not the deciding defect here, but it supplies nothing that could corroborate the trace, and POL-RD-13 expressly leaves POL-RD-10(3) governing where the trace itself is impaired.

CLAIMS ANSWERED. Both advocates' impairment claims (driver claims 1 and 5 insofar as they describe the gap; rider claims 1 and 4) are accepted: the trace is impaired and no corroboration exists. Both sides' escalation claims (driver claim 3, rider claim 4) are accepted and are the basis of this ruling. Rider claim 5 (confidence floor engaged) is accepted. Rider claim 3 and driver claim 2 (rider's POL-RD-08 burden not discharged from an independent source) are accepted. The driver's point (driver claim 5) that driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 245, and that the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags may not be substituted for it, is correct; nothing in this ruling rests on that lifetime field (POL-GEN-01).

CLAIMS CONSIDERED AND NOT REACHED. The POL-RD-02 arithmetic advanced by rider claim 6 and driver claim 6 is correct as arithmetic — 25.08 less a recomputed fare of 20.325 = 4.755, rounded up to 4.80 — but it is not reached, because the deviation it depends on cannot be established on this trace. The rider's 6.00 request is a round figure not carried by the ledger; had the deviation been proved the policy figure would be 4.80, not 6.00. Materiality and POL-RD-06 (driver claim 5, rider claim 2): the excess is above the establishment gates but below the materiality gates of 8.0 km / 50%, and no pattern exists, so no conduct uplift or POL-RD-06(c) referral arises. Pass-through lines (driver claim 7, rider claim 7): the fare breakdown carries no ERP, toll, airport-surcharge or waiting-time line, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to act on and no standalone correction or billing-integrity referral is due. The rider's own profile (rider claim 8) adds no corroboration requirement: deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, both below the POL-RD-08 thresholds.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT. The stretch that decides this case is the 450 seconds the trace is missing (14:11:30 to 14:19:00). A record-type item covering it would settle the dispute — a rider-side GPS export, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement for gantries on the corridor actually driven, or a driver statement — and a human reviewer will determine whether the missing stretch accounts for the extra distance.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
